proposals.title: Integrated Spatial Domain Discovery and Deconvolution Framework
proposals.summary: This proposal outlines a comprehensive pipeline that jointly models gene expression and spatial coordinates to identify contiguous tissue domains while addressing mixed cell populations within spots. It emphasizes robust dimensionality reduction that preserves local spatial continuity, construction of sensitivity-validated spatial graphs, and spatially aware clustering. Importantly, the approach integrates serial section alignment to maintain anatomical consistency and incorporates reference-based deconvolution techniques to infer cell-type composition in mixed spots, ensuring both biological interpretability and technical rigor.

proposals.title: Joint Modeling of Gene Expression, Spatial Alignment, and Cellular Composition
proposals.summary: This analysis plan integrates multiple challenges of spatial transcriptomics by combining domain identification with serial section registration and cell-type deconvolution. The workflow begins with modality-specific quality control and batch correction followed by a joint embedding strategy that preserves spatial continuity. A sensitivity-driven spatial graph enables robust clustering of tissue domains, while targeted deconvolution methods estimate the cellular composition of mixed capture spots. The alignment of serial sections further refines spatial domain mapping across related specimens.

proposals.title: Spatial Transcriptomic Pipeline for Domain Detection with Serial Section Registration
proposals.summary: This proposal presents an end-to-end analysis pipeline that integrates classical spatial domain identification with advanced techniques for aligning serial tissue sections. Through careful exploratory analysis, robust normalization, and weighted dimensionality reduction, the method preserves local spatial features. The pipeline further employs spatially aware clustering and graph-based metrics to validate domain continuity, while multi-section alignment ensures that anatomical structures are consistently mapped across specimens. Additional deconvolution steps are designed to unmix cell-type signals in composite spots.

proposals.title: Multi-Layered Analysis of Tissue Architecture: Domain Detection, Alignment, and Deconvolution
proposals.summary: The proposed analysis fuses three critical components of spatial transcriptomics: spatial domain identification, alignment of serial tissue sections, and cell-type deconvolution. By leveraging integrative dimensionality reduction and robust spatial graph construction, the method discriminates contiguous tissue domains while explicitly modeling local spatial continuity. The pipeline includes registration algorithms to align serial sections and utilizes reference-based deconvolution methods to deduce cellular composition within mixed spots, ensuring a holistic interpretation of tissue architecture.

proposals.title: Serial Section Integrated Domain Clustering with Cell-Type Mixture Deconvolution
proposals.summary: This framework focuses on replicability and biological insight by integrating spatial domain clustering with serial section alignment and deconvolution analysis. It features a stepwise approach: starting from rigorous quality control and normalization, the method builds a sensitivity-enhanced spatial graph to cluster gene expression profiles while preserving local continuity. Subsequent registration of serial sections allows for coherent multi-sample analysis, and dedicated deconvolution procedures infer the contributions of distinct cell types in mixed capture regions.

proposals.title: Spatial Graph-Driven Domain Identification and Cellular Decomposition
proposals.summary: In this proposal, the analysis leans on spatial graph methodologies combined with advanced deconvolution strategies to resolve tissue domains and cellular compositions simultaneously. Emphasizing sensitivity analysis, the approach constructs robust graphs that capture continuity in spatial organization, followed by spatially aware clustering to define tissue domains. Complementary deconvolution methods, informed by contextual spatial cues, estimate the cell-type contributions in mixed spots, while serial section alignment preserves sectional integrity across related samples.

proposals.title: Robust Multi-Section Alignment and Spatial Domain Characterization Workflow
proposals.summary: This analysis plan proposes a workflow that robustly identifies contiguous tissue domains and aligns serial sections to mitigate technical variability. Central to the method is a joint embedding that integrates gene expression with spatial coordinates while ensuring the preservation of local continuity. The pipeline includes explicit multi-section registration, spatial graph-based clustering, and differential expression analysis, capped by cell-type deconvolution techniques that parse mixed spots, collectively delivering biologically coherent insights.

proposals.title: Deconvolution-Enhanced Spatial Domain Discovery in Heterogeneous Tissue
proposals.summary: Addressing the challenges of spatial tissue heterogeneity, this proposal merges spatial domain discovery with deconvolution strategies to elucidate underlying cellular composition. The analytical framework integrates quality control, batch correction, and spatially weighted dimensionality reduction to effectively preserve local spatial continuity. It then applies sensitivity-validated clustering methods and registers serial sections to bolster domain mapping, culminating in targeted deconvolution to extract cell-type signals from mixed spatial spots.

proposals.title: Spatial Continuity and Cell-Type Composition Aware Analysis of Serial Tissue Sections
proposals.summary: This comprehensive approach integrates spatial transcriptomics with a focus on aligning serial sections and resolving cell-type compositions in mixed capture environments. Emphasis is placed on preserving local spatial continuity through graph-based sensitivity analysis and clustering, while robust registration techniques align multiple tissue sections. The pipeline incorporates deconvolution algorithms that leverage both gene expression and spatial context to accurately estimate cell-type proportions, facilitating a deeper understanding of tissue organization.

proposals.title: Integrated Pipeline for Spatial Domain, Cellular Deconvolution, and Serial Section Alignment
proposals.summary: This proposal articulates an integrated computational framework that unifies spatial domain identification, cellular deconvolution, and serial section alignment. The method utilizes joint modeling of gene expression and spatial coordinates to maintain local continuity and employs sensitivity analysis to construct reliable spatial graphs. It further embeds serial section registration to standardize tissue architecture across samples, while reference-based deconvolution techniques are incorporated to resolve the cell-type composition of mixed spots, yielding a multidimensional view of tissue organization.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to propose exactly 10 computational spatial-omics analyses likely performed in the hidden paper, producing draft, critique, and final proposal JSON artifacts without executing the analyses.

steps.title: Draft spatial analysis proposals
steps.description: Use the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) to generate an initial set of 10 computational spatial-omics analysis proposals, based solely on the provided background about spatial transcriptomics. The agent will write these as a structured JSON draft to `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json`, capturing for each candidate a tentative title and descriptive summary focused on jointly modeling expression and geometry, spatial domains, section alignment, and spatially aware deconvolution/composition, without running any analyses.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated spatial planning agent is required to translate the generic background on spatial transcriptomics into a coherent, diverse draft set of 10 plausible analyses that a paper could perform, while respecting constraints like joint expression-geometry representation and multi-section integration. This draft becomes the foundation that later critique and synthesis will refine.
steps.assignment_rationale: The user explicitly requires the Spatial-CV Planning Agent for drafting exactly 10 spatial-omics analysis proposals, and this agent is specialized for creating draft proposal sets (including spatially focused CV-style variants).

steps.title: Critique draft proposal set
steps.description: Have the Critic-style agent load `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and evaluate each of the 10 draft analyses for clarity, plausibility, distinctness, and alignment with the stated challenges (spatial domain identification, alignment across sections, cell-type composition in mixed spots, and preserving local continuity). The agent will not execute analyses or score against hidden answers, but will produce a structured critique with per-proposal comments and global suggestions, saved to `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`.
steps.reasoning: A separate critique step ensures the draft proposals are systematically reviewed for overlap, missing aspects of the background (e.g., multi-organ or multi-platform integration), and potential misalignment with the spatial-omics challenges, providing actionable feedback that can guide a stronger final synthesis.
steps.assignment_rationale: The critic_agent is designed solely for reviewing and critiquing candidate spatial paper analyses and for writing a critique JSON artifact, matching the needs of the draft evaluation step.

steps.title: Synthesize final proposal collection
steps.description: Using both `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`, a synthesis/Hypothesis-style agent will construct the final set of exactly 10 refined computational spatial-omics analyses most consistent with the background text. The agent will revise, merge, or replace draft items as needed (without executing any analysis) and write `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` as a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, mapped to an array of exactly 10 objects, each containing only `title` and a detailed `summary` describing the proposed analysis at a conceptual level.
steps.reasoning: This final synthesis step is needed to convert the critiqued draft into the required benchmark deliverable: a single, clean JSON file of 10 well-justified analysis proposals, all grounded in the spatial transcriptomics background and covering spatial domains, cross-section alignment, spatially aware deconvolution, and joint expression-geometry representations, without introducing extra metadata or running any computations on real data.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is responsible for final synthesis of exactly 10 spatial analysis hypotheses into a structured proposals JSON, aligning with the required final_proposals.json output format.

provenance.justification: The paper_hypothesis_generation template was adapted conceptually for its draft→critique→final pattern, but simplified to three steps and retargeted to spatial-omics analysis proposal generation. We discarded its PDF/dataset inventory steps and its specific file paths, and instead aligned the plan to the user-mandated artifacts (draft_proposals.json, critique.json, final_proposals.json) and to the spatial transcriptomics background, ensuring that the template itself is not used as a candidate analysis.
